title: Heat Hazards — WBGT workload and acclimatization guidance (OSHA)
publisher: U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration
claims: WBGT integrates four heat-stress factors: temperature, humidity, radiant heat from the sun or other sources, and wind speed.
Heat stress limits are published as WBGT ranges split by workload level: light, moderate, heavy or very heavy.
Workers are assumed unacclimatized if they have been doing the job for less than one to two weeks; acclimatization must be built up over repeated heat exposure.
The heat index is a WBGT substitute that accounts for temperature and humidity, but it does not account for radiant heat or wind speed.
